# Maggaṅgavibhaṅga (Vb 11)
**ID:** Vb 11
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma

**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/vb11

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* (Vb 11) is the eleventh chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text is dedicated to the analytical exposition of the path factors (*maggaṅga*) that constitute the Noble Eightfold Path. In traditional Burmese scholasticism, Ledi Sayadaw groups the *Maggaṅgavibhaṅga* alongside the *Satipaṭṭhāna-*, *Sammappadhāna-*, *Iddhipāda-*, *Indriya-*, and *Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgas* as comprehensive analytical treatises expounding the characteristics, development, and fruition of the requisites of enlightenment (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) for practitioners in need of formal guidance (*neyya*) [Ledi Sayadaw 2007]. In comparative Abhidharma scholarship, Erich Frauwallner notes that chapter 11, together with chapters 15 and 16, represents an addition in the *Vibhaṅga* beyond the older doctrinal list (*mātṛkā*) shared between the Theravāda *Vibhaṅga* and the Sarvāstivāda *Dharmaskandha* [Frauwallner 1995].
According to SuttaCentral, one translation is cataloged for this text [SuttaCentral]. Machine alignment by DharmaNexus reveals extensive internal reuse within the Pali canon (over 4,200 matches across 147 texts). The closest textual partners in the Abhidhamma are the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (especially the *Lokuttaravipāka* and *Lokuttarakusala* sections, Ds 2.1.8 and Ds 2.1.5) and related Vibhaṅga treatises, particularly the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), where the path factors are defined under the fourth noble truth, as well as the *Satipaṭṭhāna-* (Vb 7), *Iddhipāda-* (Vb 9), *Bojjhaṅga-* (Vb 10), and *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 8) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, the text shares significant segment clusters with the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45) and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (*Ñāṇakathā*, Ps 1.1) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistic matches identified by DharmaNexus include Sanskrit doctrinal expositions such as the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and its commentary (*Nibandhana*), Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and the *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*; Chinese Āgama discourses in the *Madhyama-āgama* (T 26) and *Saṃyukta-āgama* (T 99); and Tibetan versions of the *Arthaviniścaya* (D 317) and *Bodhisattvapiṭaka* (D 56) [DharmaNexus].
